Use this to check the exact project names in your journal. Reuse a name to keep related entries together.

## CLI: gournal projects

List every project that you log to, with the number of entries for each project.

```text
gournal projects
```

## MCP tool: list_projects

List every project in the journal, with the number of entries for each project.

### Input

This tool takes no input.

### Output

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|-------|------|----------|-------------|
| `projects` | `object[]` | yes | Projects, most entries first. |
| `projects.project` | `string` | yes | Project name. |
| `projects.count` | `number` | yes | Number of entries in this project. |

## Examples

### CLI

List every project with its number of entries.

```console
$ gournal projects
billing-api  5
worker  3
```

### MCP

List every project with its number of entries. The tool takes no input.

```json
{}
```

The structured result:

```json
{
  "projects": [
    {
      "project": "billing-api",
      "count": 5
    },
    {
      "project": "worker",
      "count": 3
    }
  ]
}
```

The text result holds the `projects` list as JSON.
